newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan to cut back Asian outlets in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan to cut back Asian outlets in restructuring.

text.p: Japan's Yaohan retailing group announced a broad restructuring plan on Monday under which it will scale back its presence in Southeast Asia, cut its managers' salaries and try to trim its debt.

Yaohan will close one of its Singapore stores in June, sell part of its stake in a Malaysian affiliate and relaunch one of its Thai stores as a wholesale facility, the group's flagship company Yaohan Japan said.

The group, which runs a chain of medium-sized supermarkets and department stores in Asia, Europe and the United States, will also freeze or postpone plans to open new outlets in Japan, where it now has 135 stores.

Yaohan said the retrenchment followed "excessive" investment both at home and overseas, but added that it had resolved any immediate cash flow problems with the cooperation of its banks and suppliers.

Like other Japanese retail chains, Yaohan expanded overseas in search of new and expanding markets but was more aggressive in its push offshore, even moving its group corporate headquarters outside Japan. The headquarters were moved to Hong Kong in 1990 and then to Shanghai in April this year.
"Our investments, both domestic and overseas, have been excessive," Terumasa Wada, president of Yaohan Japan, told a Tokyo news conference.
But Yaohan Japan chairman Kazuo Wada said the company would press on with its planned expansion in China.
Under its austerity plan, the company will cut the salaries of its senior executives by between 15 and 50 percent, with its chairman and president taking the biggest pay cuts.
Executive bonuses for board members will also be halted and the number of board members will be cut to 10 from the current 17, Yaohan said.
The company also said it planned to slim down total assets and reduce debts.
Yaohan Japan said it redeemed warrant bonds earlier this month with the help of banks.
It also said its Japanese suppliers had agreed to a request to extend the time lag between merchandise delivery and payment to two months from the current one month.
The news last week that Yaohan had requested a longer grace period had sparked worries among investors that the company may be facing financial problems, pushing down its share price.
Yaohan Japan shares were lifted by the restructuring news on Monday, rising four yen to close at 470 yen ($4.12). ($1=114 yen)
